1.
Heard Mr. D. K. Bhattacharyya learned counsel for the Applicant.
Also heard Mr. K. K. Parasar learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State respondent as well as Mr. S. Nawaz, learned Legal Aid Counsel representing the informant.
2. This interlocutory application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, Page No.# 3/5 1963, praying for condoning the delay of 183 days in preferring the connected appeal by the present applicant.

3. By filing the connected appeal, the applicant intend to impugn the judgment and order dated 06.04.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge cum Special Judge (POCSO),
Morigaon, in POCSO Case No.71/2019, whereby the applicant is convicted under Section 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and has been sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 (ten) years and also to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- in default stipulation and also he is convicted under Section 366 of the Indian penal code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7(seven) years and also to pay a fine of Rs.7,000/- and in default of payment of fine to suffer further imprisonment for Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62687318/
2 3 months against that offence.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the delay has been caused as the applicant was detained after the delivery of the judgment and being poor and having no financial means to engage a counsel, he could not pursue his appeal before this Court.
5. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the family members were also ignorant about the rights of the appellant and were not knowing that an appeal may be preferred.

They were informed about their rights only when a legal aid camp was organized by a NGO called Studio NILIMA in the Morigaon district jail and thereafter, only the plight of the appellant came to the light.
6.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the delay in filing the connected appeal was caused only due to poverty as well as ignorance of the applicant and his family members.

7. Learned Additional Public prosecutor as well as learned Legal Aid Page No.# 4/5 Counsel for the informant considering the cause shown by the applicant for the delay in preferring the connected appeal raised no objection against condoning the delay.

8. However, Mr. K. K. Parasar learned Additional Public Prosecutor has pointed out that the supporting affidavit in this application has been sworn by one Ms. Maina Devi, who is the wife of the applicant and her age has been shown as 61 years which may not be correct age.

On this learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the age as mentioned in the affidavit may not be correct age and same should be typographical mistake as the applicant's wife is not more than 32 years of age.
9. He undertakes to furnish a fresh affidavit within a period of 15 days from the date of this order.

10. I have also perused the affidavit, the same appears to be typographical mistake as submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant and it does not affect merit of the instant application and as the prayer for condonation of delay has not been opposed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor as well as the Legal Aid Counsel representing the informant, the typographical error in the affidavit would not affect the merit of this case.
11.

Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for both the sides as well as considering the cause shown in the paragraph 8 of the Interlocutory Application, this Court is of the considered opinion that delay of preferring the connected appeal has been sufficiently explained by the applicant.
12. Hence, the said delay is hereby condoned and this Interlocutory Application is allowed subject to what has been stated herein above.

14. List accordingly.
